cyp_mechanism: Pharmacodynamic additive serotonergic enhancement & CYP3A4/CYP2C19 induction
clinical_effect: Severe risk of Serotonin Syndrome manifested by hyperthermia, ocular and neuromuscular clonus, severe tremors, autonomic instability, and potentially fatal delirium.
management_recommendation: Contraindicated. Strictly avoid concomitant administration; enforce a mandatory 14-day washout period between discontinuation of St. John's Wort and initiation of SSRIs.

cyp_mechanism: Potent transcriptional upregulation of hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 and MDR1 (P-glycoprotein) via PXR nuclear receptor activation
clinical_effect: Substantial decrease (50-70%) in circulating cyclosporine blood levels resulting in sub-therapeutic trough concentrations and acute allograft organ transplant rejection.
management_recommendation: Contraindicated. Prohibit St. John's Wort use in all solid organ transplant recipients. Monitor blood trough levels immediately if accidental co-administration occurs.

cyp_mechanism: Induction of hepatic CYP3A4 and glucuronosyltransferases accelerating estrogen and progestin clearance
clinical_effect: Breakthrough bleeding, rapid reduction in circulating contraceptive steroid levels, ovulatory breakthrough, and unexpected pregnancy.
management_recommendation: Contraindicated. Advise patients taking St. John's Wort to switch to non-hormonal barrier contraception or discontinue herbal self-medication.

cyp_mechanism: Induction of intestinal ABCB1 / MDR1 (P-glycoprotein) efflux pump expression
clinical_effect: Significant decrease (up to 33%) in serum digoxin area under the curve (AUC), resulting in loss of ventricular rate control in atrial fibrillation and decompensated heart failure.
management_recommendation: Contraindicated. Avoid concomitant use; if herbal therapy is ceased, monitor digoxin levels closely to prevent rebound toxicity as P-glycoprotein induction decays.

cyp_mechanism: Ginkgolide B platelet-activating factor (PAF) receptor antagonism coupled with mild CYP2C9 modulation
clinical_effect: Spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage, retroperitoneal hematoma, and ocular hyphema without necessarily altering INR, due to concurrent platelet inhibition and factor synthesis reduction.
management_recommendation: Contraindicated. Avoid co-administration. Discontinue Ginkgo biloba at least 7 to 10 days prior to elective surgery or dental procedures.

cyp_mechanism: Dual antiplatelet cascade inhibition: COX-1 thromboxane A2 suppression paired with Ginkgolide B PAF antagonism
clinical_effect: Marked prolongation of template bleeding time, excessive spontaneous ecchymosis, severe epistaxis, and gastrointestinal hemorrhage.
management_recommendation: Avoid combination. Educate patients on bleeding risks and advise routine physician disclosure before starting herbal cognitive supplements.

cyp_mechanism: Inhibition of platelet cyclooxygenase and thromboxane synthetase by allicin, ajoene, and diallyl trisulfide
clinical_effect: Additive antiplatelet action leading to increased bleeding propensity and spontaneous hematoma formation during anticoagulation therapy.
management_recommendation: Caution. High-dose garlic supplements (>4 cloves or >1000 mg aged garlic extract daily) should be discontinued 7 days before surgery or in patients on warfarin.

cyp_mechanism: Intestinal P-glycoprotein induction and CYP3A4 upregulation reducing oral bioavailability
clinical_effect: Approximately 50% decrease in saquinavir AUC and Cmax, threatening virologic breakthrough and the emergence of antiretroviral resistance.
management_recommendation: Avoid concurrent use of high-dose garlic capsules with protease inhibitors; dietary consumption in normal culinary quantities remains acceptable.

cyp_mechanism: Weak hepatic CYP2C9 and CYP1A2 induction by ginsenosides, accelerating S-warfarin clearance
clinical_effect: Clinically confirmed reduction in international normalized ratio (INR) and decreased peak warfarin plasma concentrations, elevating thrombosis risk.
management_recommendation: Avoid combination. If patients insist on using ginseng, conduct serial INR monitoring every 48-72 hours until stable anticoagulation is established.

cyp_mechanism: Central nervous system stimulant synergism and monoaminergic potentiation
clinical_effect: Manic symptoms, visual hallucinations, insomnia, tremulousness, and severe hypertensive crisis.
management_recommendation: Contraindicated. Prohibit co-administration of Panax ginseng or eleuthero products in patients maintained on MAO inhibitor therapy.

cyp_mechanism: Glycyrrhetinic acid inhibition of renal 11beta-HSD2 producing pseudoaldosteronism
clinical_effect: Direct pharmacological antagonism of spironolactone's natriuretic activity, resulting in uncontrolled hypertension, sodium retention, and unpredictable potassium flux.
management_recommendation: Contraindicated. Patients undergoing treatment for hypertension or heart failure must eliminate glycyrrhizin-containing confectionery and extracts; recommend DGL (deglycyrrhizinated licorice).

cyp_mechanism: 11beta-HSD2 inhibition leading to profound renal potassium wasting and hypokalemia
clinical_effect: Hypokalemia dramatically sensitizes the myocardial myocardium to digoxin, predisposing patients to fatal ventricular bigeminy, ventricular tachycardia, and cardiac arrest.
management_recommendation: Contraindicated. Prohibit glycyrrhizin intake in patients taking cardiac glycosides. Immediate electrolyte panel check is mandatory upon suspected co-ingestion.

cyp_mechanism: Mild in-vitro inhibition of CYP2C9 and hepatic UGT1A1 by silymarin flavonolignans
clinical_effect: Marginal increase in losartan plasma levels with minimal alteration to its active carboxylic acid metabolite (E-3174) or baseline blood pressure.
management_recommendation: Monitor. Generally safe at standard therapeutic doses (140-420 mg silymarin); routine clinical monitoring of blood pressure is sufficient.

cyp_mechanism: Kavalactones bind to GABAA receptor subtypes and inhibit CYP2E1/CYP3A4 clearance
clinical_effect: Synergistic central nervous system depression, marked lethargy, ataxia, stupor, and clinical coma requiring emergency hospitalization.
management_recommendation: Contraindicated. Strictly prohibit concurrent use of kava with benzodiazepines, barbiturates, or sedating antihistamines.

cyp_mechanism: Additive pharmacodynamic allosteric modulation of GABAA receptor beta subunits by valerenic acid
clinical_effect: Excessive daytime drowsiness, impaired motor coordination, cognitive psychomotor slowing, and prolonged sedation.
management_recommendation: Avoid combination. Counsel patients against co-ingesting valerian extracts with prescription hypnotics; warn against operating heavy machinery.

cyp_mechanism: Inhibition of intestinal CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein transport by high-dose bioenhanced curcumin formulations
clinical_effect: Elevated blood tacrolimus trough concentrations predisposing to nephrotoxicity, neurotoxicity, tremors, and electrolyte imbalances.
management_recommendation: Caution. Patients on immunosuppressive regimens should avoid high-potency curcumin extracts (especially piperine-enhanced preparations); monitor trough levels regularly.

cyp_mechanism: Mild thrombin and platelet aggregation inhibition combined with weak CYP2C9 metabolic interference
clinical_effect: Potential elevation in INR and enhanced bleeding risk; spontaneous bruising and hematuria reported in case studies.
management_recommendation: Monitor. Limit turmeric consumption to standard culinary spice levels; avoid high-dose therapeutic curcumin supplements without hematological supervision.

cyp_mechanism: Withanolides stimulate endogenous thyroid hormone synthesis (T3 and T4) via hypothalamic-pituitary-thyroid axis modulation
clinical_effect: Additive thyroid elevation precipitating iatrogenic thyrotoxicosis: palpitations, heat intolerance, tremors, anxiety, and suppressed TSH.
management_recommendation: Caution. Monitor thyroid function panels (TSH, Free T3, Free T4) within 4-6 weeks if ashwagandha is introduced in patients taking levothyroxine.

cyp_mechanism: GABA-mimetic activity of withanolides augmenting central GABAA chloride conductance
clinical_effect: Additive central nervous system depression, profound sedation, impaired psychomotor reflexes, and daytime somnolence.
management_recommendation: Avoid concurrent use. Advise patients tapering or taking benzodiazepines that ashwagandha can unpredictably compound sedation.

cyp_mechanism: Epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG) potently inhibits intestinal influx transporter OATP1A2 (Organic Anion Transporting Polypeptide 1A2)
clinical_effect: Severe reduction (up to 85%) in plasma nadolol concentrations, leading to blunted antihypertensive response and inadequate heart rate control.
management_recommendation: Separate administration. Advise patients taking nadolol to avoid green tea beverages or EGCG supplements within 4 hours of dosing.

cyp_mechanism: High dietary vitamin K1 (phylloquinone) content in brewed green tea antagonizing warfarin mechanism of action
clinical_effect: Significant decrease in INR values predisposing to deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, or stroke in anticoagulated individuals.
management_recommendation: Maintain consistency. Advise patients to keep their daily green tea intake constant rather than drastically increasing or eliminating consumption.

botanical_name: Coptis chinensis Franch. / Hydrastis canadensis L.
cyp_mechanism: Potent mechanism-based competitive and irreversible inhibition of intestinal and hepatic CYP3A4/5 by berberine
clinical_effect: Approximately 40-60% increase in midazolam AUC and prolongation of elimination half-life, causing exaggerated and prolonged clinical sedation.
management_recommendation: Contraindicated. Discontinue berberine supplements prior to procedural sedation involving CYP3A substrates.

cyp_mechanism: Dual AMPK activation and OCT1 / OCT2 (Organic Cation Transporters) competitive inhibition
clinical_effect: Additive blood glucose lowering increasing hypoglycemia episodes; potential alteration in renal metformin clearance and gastrointestinal cramps.
management_recommendation: Monitor blood glucose closely. May require metformin dose titration under endocrinologist guidance when berberine is co-administered.

cyp_mechanism: Bidirectional modulation of CYP2B6 and CYP3A4 by artemisinin and efavirenz auto-induction
clinical_effect: Decreased plasma concentrations of artemisinin derivatives and potential fluctuations in NNRTI efficacy, risking subtherapeutic antimalarial response.
management_recommendation: Caution. Utilize standard WHO-endorsed Artemisinin-based Combination Therapies (ACTs) with rigorous clinical monitoring; avoid unregulated home artemisia teas.

cyp_mechanism: Inhibition of CYP3A4 isozymes by pentacyclic oxindole alkaloids
clinical_effect: Elevated protease inhibitor plasma levels resulting in increased incidence of hyperbilirubinemia, jaundice, gastrointestinal intolerance, and nephrolithiasis.
management_recommendation: Avoid combination. HIV patients receiving antiretroviral regimens should refrain from using Cat's Claw extracts.

cyp_mechanism: Mild inhibition of CYP2C9 combined with purpura-inducing cyclooxygenase attenuation
clinical_effect: Unexplained purpura, elevated INR, and spontaneous soft tissue hematomas in patients stabilized on warfarin.
management_recommendation: Caution. Monitor INR within 7 days of starting or stopping Devil's claw supplementation.

cyp_mechanism: Pharmacodynamic immune stimulation: immunostimulatory alkamides and arabinogalactans stimulate T-cell and macrophage proliferation
clinical_effect: Direct antagonism of immunosuppressive therapy; potential triggering of graft-versus-host reaction or organ rejection in transplant recipients.
management_recommendation: Contraindicated. Patients taking systemic immunosuppressants or suffering from autoimmune diseases (lupus, MS, RA) should not take Echinacea.

cyp_mechanism: Additive central and peripheral competitive antagonism at muscarinic acetylcholine receptors
clinical_effect: Precipitation of severe Anticholinergic Toxidrome: hyperthermia, anhydrosis, flushing, urinary retention, bowel ileus, mydriasis, delirium, and coma.
management_recommendation: Contraindicated. Never combine belladonna preparations with prescription or OTC antihistamines, tricyclic antidepressants, or antimuscarinics.

cyp_mechanism: Synergistic sympathetic amine depletion: reserpine depletes cardiac norepinephrine while beta-blockers block adrenergic receptors
clinical_effect: Profound bradycardia, complete atrioventricular (AV) heart block, severe orthostatic hypotension, syncope, and congestive cardiac arrest.
management_recommendation: Contraindicated. Avoid concomitant administration. If both classes were co-prescribed, execute gradual tapering with continuous telemetry monitoring.

cyp_mechanism: Pharmacodynamic electrolyte perturbation: loop diuretics induce renal kaluresis and hypokalemia
clinical_effect: Extracellular hypokalemia enhances digitalis binding to myocardial Na+/K+-ATPase, triggering deadly digitalis toxicity, ventricular arrhythmias, and asystole.
management_recommendation: Contraindicated in crude herbal form. In pharmaceutical cardiology, loop diuretics require aggressive potassium monitoring and potassium chloride supplementation.
